AbstractText.Label: Background
AbstractText.content: Interleukin-1 (IL-1), an important proinflammatory cytokine, is suspected to play a role in chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS).

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the effect of subcutaneous anakinra versus placebo on fatigue severity in female patients with CFS.

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial from July 2014 to May 2016. Patients, providers, and researchers were blinded to treatment assignment. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02108210).

AbstractText.Label: Patients
AbstractText.content: 50 women aged 18 to 59 years with CFS and severe fatigue leading to functional impairment.

AbstractText.Label: Intervention
AbstractText.content: Participants were randomly assigned to daily subcutaneous anakinra, 100 mg (n = 25), or placebo (n = 25) for 4 weeks and were followed for an additional 20 weeks after treatment (n = 50).

AbstractText.Label: Measurements
AbstractText.content: The primary outcome was fatigue severity, measured by the Checklist Individual Strength subscale (CIS-fatigue) at 4 weeks. Secondary outcomes were level of impairment, physical and social functioning, psychological distress, and pain severity at 4 and 24 weeks.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: At 4 weeks, 8% (2 of 25) of anakinra recipients and 20% (5 of 25) of placebo recipients reached a fatigue level within the range reported by healthy persons. There were no clinically important or statistically significant differences between groups in CIS-fatigue score at 4 weeks (mean difference, 1.5 points [95% CI, -4.1 to 7.2 points]) or the end of follow-up. No statistically significant between-group differences were seen for any secondary outcome at 4 weeks or the end of follow-up. One patient in the anakinra group discontinued treatment because of an adverse event. Patients in the anakinra group had more injection site reactions (68% [17 of 25] vs. 4% [1 of 25]).

AbstractText.Label: Limitation
AbstractText.content: Small sample size and wide variability in symptom duration; inclusion was not limited to patients with postinfectious symptoms.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusion
AbstractText.content: Peripheral IL-1 inhibition using anakinra for 4 weeks does not result in a clinically significant reduction in fatigue severity in women with CFS and severe fatigue.

AbstractText.Label: Primary Funding Source
AbstractText.content: Interleukin Foundation and an independent donor who wishes to remain anonymous.
